# Hand-marked cadences in Clementi, Sonatina in C major, Op. 36 No. 1, first movement.
#
# SOURCE: the IMSLP scan of the first edition (Op. 36, 1797) and a modern urtext of the Op. 36 sonatinas.
# STATUS: VERIFIED against an edition by Michelle Opitz, 2026-10-17. Read from the MIDI first and checked against standard theory and a printed edition (R-092). The numerals and cadences are a hand reading of the
# harmony, made from the pitch content of tests/fixtures/framework-v1-corpus/"Clementi 36.mid" (notes dumped beat by beat) and
# the piece's known form. They were NOT derived from the output of the chord identifier, the key estimator or the
# cadence adapter.
#
# The reading follows standard-harmony's definitions, not every analyst's: a PAC or IAC is a root-position V (or V7)
# to a root-position I, so a V6 or V4/3 to I is not marked (it prolongs); viio to I is not a cadence; a half cadence
# arrives on a root-position V after a tonic or predominant (an applied chord before it does not count); and a
# plagal IV-I is a cadence only directly after a PAC. A cadence on a weak offbeat is marked where the music puts it,
# even though the adapter looks only for arrivals on at least a medium beat.
#
# FORMAT, one per line (lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored):
#   meter <beats per measure> <beat length as a fraction of a whole note>   e.g. 3 1/4 (3/4), 4 3/8 (12/8)
#   home <tonic>              the piece's key (major), for the whole-chain run: C Db D Eb E F F# G Ab A Bb B
#   chord <measure> <beat> <tonic> <numeral>   a chord of the hand analysis, in the major key on <tonic>, sounding
#                             until the next chord line (or the end line); beats are 1-based, a half beat is .5;
#                             numerals are ASCII: V7, ii6, V4/3, I6/4, viio/V (an applied chord is a slash and the
#                             degree it tonicizes)
#   end <measure> <beat>      the end of the stretch of chords (chords outside a stretch are not read)
#   cadence <measure> <beat> <pac|iac|hc|deceptive|plagal|subverted>   the cadence whose ARRIVAL chord starts here
#
# The cadence of the recapitulated main theme (measures 30-31) and the closing cadence of the movement (measures 36-38). Earlier cadences have
# inverted dominants (V4/3 over D, V4/2 over F) and are not marked, by the definition above. In m30 the cadential 6/4 (G in the bass under C and E) resolves
# to V on beat 4, and m31 arrives on I with C in the bass and the soprano; the scale that follows in m31 links to the second theme.

meter 4 1/4
home C
chord 30 1 C I6/4
chord 30 4 C V
chord 31 1 C I
end 32 1
chord 36 1 C IV
chord 37 1 C V7
chord 38 1 C I
end 39 1
cadence 31 1 pac
cadence 38 1 pac
